proofs.proof_tex:
Fix the effective \(K\)-valued matrices \(B,Q\), the supplied graph \(G\), and the known integer \(m\geq 2\).  Put
\[
 \mathcal I_G
 =\{(i,i):i\in V\}\cup
   \{(i,j):j<i\text{ and }j\to i\text{ in }G\}.
\]
For every \((i,j)\in\mathcal I_G\), introduce a real variable \(a_{ij}\), and introduce real variables \(d_1,\ldots,d_d\).  Let \(\widetilde A(a)\) have entry \(a_{ij}\) on \(\mathcal I_G\) and zero elsewhere, and let \(\widetilde D(d)=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_d)\).  Thus the lower-triangular and graph-support restrictions in the definition of \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\) are imposed by the coordinate parametrization itself.

Consider the finite system
\[
 \bigl[\widetilde A(a)^m\bigr]_{ij}=B_{ij}
 \quad(i,j\in V),                                                   \tag{1}
\]
\[
 \left[\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}\widetilde A(a)^r\widetilde D(d)
                    \bigl(\widetilde A(a)^r\bigr)^\top\right]_{ij}
 =Q_{ij}
 \quad(i,j\in V),                                                   \tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 -1<a_{ii}<1\quad(i\in V),
 \qquad d_i>0\quad(i\in V).                                        \tag{3}
\]
Every left-hand side in (1)--(2) is a polynomial in finitely many variables with coefficients in \(K\), by the effective-input assumption.  Since \(\widetilde A(a)\) is triangular,
\[
 \det\{\lambda I-\widetilde A(a)\}
   =\prod_{i=1}^d(\lambda-a_{ii}),
 \qquad
 \rho\{\widetilde A(a)\}=\max_i|a_{ii}|.
\]
Consequently the first collection of strict inequalities in (3) is equivalent to stability.  Moreover, for every nonzero \(x\in\mathbb R^d\),
\[
 x^\top\widetilde D(d)x=\sum_{i=1}^d d_i x_i^2>0
\]
if and only if every \(d_i>0\).  Hence the second collection in (3) is equivalent to \(\widetilde D(d)\succ0\).  It follows directly from the definition of the compatible fiber that
\[
 (a,d)\longmapsto\bigl(\widetilde A(a),\widetilde D(d)\bigr)         \tag{4}
\]
is a bijection from the realization of (1)--(3) onto \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\).  In particular, this encoding neither adds boundary points nor replaces strict positivity or strict stability by their closures.

For a triangular matrix, the diagonal part of (1) is
\[
 a_{ii}^{,m}=B_{ii},\qquad i\in V.                                 \tag{5}
\]
The effective real-closed-field operations enumerate the real roots of each equation (5) and decide the strict inequalities in (3).  There is exactly one real root of \(x^m=b\) when \(m\) is odd; when \(m\) is even there are zero, one, or two real roots according as \(b<0\), \(b=0\), or \(b>0\).  Thus there are finitely many surviving diagonal branches, all represented exactly in \(K\).  If none survives, (4) shows already that the compatible fiber is empty.

Fix one surviving branch and process off-diagonal pairs \((v,u)\) in increasing order of \(v-u\), as prescribed by the graph-recursive root map.  The path-expansion lemma gives
\[
 a_{vu}C_m(a_{vv},a_{uu})
   =B_{vu}-R_{vu,m}(\widetilde A(a)).                                \tag{6}
\]
Every off-diagonal coordinate occurring on the right side of (6) has smaller endpoint gap.  The diagonal entries in
\[
 c_{vu}:=C_m(a_{vv},a_{uu})                                         \tag{7}
\]
are fixed on the branch, so \(c_{vu}\in K\).  The divided-difference zero-set lemma, together with the exact sign tests in \(K\), decides whether \(c_{vu}=0\); importantly, it retains the odd-factor case \(a_{vv}=a_{uu}=0\) and the even-factor case \(a_{vv}=-a_{uu}\) as singular cases.

If \(v\leftarrow u\) is graph-allowed and \(c_{vu}\neq0\), equation (6) is equivalent to the unique substitution
\[
 a_{vu}
 =\frac{B_{vu}-R_{vu,m}(\widetilde A(a))}{c_{vu}}.                  \tag{8}
\]
This is the only division in the recursion, and it is made only after the nonzero test.  Because \(c_{vu}^{-1}\in K\) is a fixed coefficient on the branch, substitution of (8) into the later transition and covariance equations produces polynomials over \(K\) in the residual variables; it introduces no variable denominator.  If \(c_{vu}=0\), the coordinate is not eliminated and the induced equation
\[
 B_{vu}-R_{vu,m}(\widetilde A(a))=0                                \tag{9}
\]
is retained.  If the edge is forbidden, \(a_{vu}=0\) by the support parametrization and the transition equation (9) is likewise retained, regardless of the value of \(c_{vu}\).

Induction over the endpoint gap now proves exactness of the recursion.  Indeed, at a nonsingular allowed coordinate every solution of the pre-substitution system must have the value (8), and every solution of the substituted system lifts uniquely by (8); at a singular or forbidden coordinate no variable or equation needed for compatibility is discarded.  After the finitely many pairs have been processed, all unprocessed transition equations, all covariance equations (2), and all strict inequalities (3) remain imposed after the accumulated substitutions.  Therefore, if \(\mathfrak R_b\) denotes the residual semialgebraic realization on diagonal branch \(b\), reconstruction gives
\[
 \mathcal S(B,Q;G)
   =\bigcup_b \operatorname{Rec}_b(\mathfrak R_b),                 \tag{10}
\]
where equality is literal, not merely equality after closure or Zariski completion.

Each \(\mathfrak R_b\) is a finite Boolean combination of polynomial equalities and strict polynomial inequalities over \(K\).  There are finitely many branches and finitely many variables.  The effective CAD decision-and-sampling lemma therefore implies that CAD terminates on every branch, decides whether \(\mathfrak R_b\) is empty, and returns an exact represented point when it is nonempty.  By (10), all branch systems are empty if and only if \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)=\varnothing\).  This proves termination, soundness, and completeness of the incompatibility output.

It remains to prove that the other two outputs classify the transfer fiber exactly.  Suppose the compatible fiber is nonempty, and take two compatible points.  Write
\[
 p=A_{vu},\quad q=A_{vv},\qquad
 p'=A'_{vu},\quad q'=A'_{vv}.
\]
Stability gives \(|q|<1\) and \(|q'|<1\).  Hence, for every \(z\in\mathbb T\),
\[
 |qz|<1,\qquad |q'z|<1,
\]
so neither \(1-qz\) nor \(1-q'z\) vanishes.  Cross multiplication is therefore valid, and the two transfers agree on \(\mathbb T\) if and only if
\[
 p(1-q'z)=p'(1-qz)\quad\text{for every }z\in\mathbb T.             \tag{11}
\]
The difference between the sides of (11) is
\[
 (p-p')+(p'q-pq')z.                                                  \tag{12}
\]
Evaluating (12) at \(z=1\) and \(z=-1\) shows that it vanishes on \(\mathbb T\) if and only if both of its coefficients vanish.  Thus
\[
 h_{p,q}=h_{p',q'}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 p=p'\ \text{ and }\ pq'=p'q                                      \tag{13}
\]
and, because all quantities are real,
\[
 h_{p,q}\neq h_{p',q'}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \Delta(p,q,p',q')
 :=(p-p')^2+(pq'-p'q)^2>0.                                         \tag{14}
\]
Notice that (13) correctly identifies all pairs \((0,q)\) with the same zero transfer; equality of the coefficient pair itself is not incorrectly required.

For each ordered pair of diagonal branches, take two copies of the corresponding complete residual systems and append the strict polynomial inequality (14), after reconstruction.  The finite union of these two-copy systems is feasible if and only if there exist two points of \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\) having unequal transfers, by (10) and (14).  The CAD lemma decides this feasibility and, when it holds, supplies exact residual sample points.  Reconstruction produces attained pairs
\[
 (A,D),(A',D')\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)
\]
satisfying the strict inequality in the theorem.  Their strict diagonal and innovation inequalities are inherited from their branch systems, so they are stable and have positive diagonal innovation covariance.  This proves soundness of the ambiguity output, while feasibility equivalence proves its completeness.

If every two-copy system is infeasible, (14) says that every two compatible points yield the same transfer.  A sample from any nonempty one-copy branch then provides a pair \((p,q)\) and the common exact rational function
\[
 z\longmapsto\frac{pz}{1-qz}.
\]
Conversely, if the transfer fiber is a singleton, no two-copy system can satisfy (14), so the certificate returns this common function.  This establishes both directions of the singleton assertion.

All advertised exceptional cases are included in the preceding equivalences.  Zero diagonal roots are retained in (5) and are sent to the singular residual system whenever the divided difference vanishes.  A forbidden queried edge, or an allowed queried edge forced to zero by compatibility, is handled by (13).  Open and positive-dimensional fibers are handled directly by the cited CAD lemma with the strict inequalities (3).  Branch duplication or merger cannot affect the answer because (10) is a union and the two-copy test ranges over every ordered branch pair.  No rank, overlap, conditioning, or limiting premise is used, and no division is made without the explicit nonzero condition in (8).

Finally, the two requested destructive checks agree with the certificate.  For \(d=2\), \(m=3\), the graph containing \(1\to2\), \(B=0\), and \(Q=I_2\), define
\[
 A_{\pm}=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\ \pm\tfrac12&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 D_{\pm}=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(1,\tfrac34\right).
\]
Then \(A_{\pm}^2=0\), and hence
\[
 A_{\pm}^3=0=B,
 \qquad
 \sum_{r=0}^{2}A_{\pm}^rD_{\pm}(A_{\pm}^r)^\top
 =D_{\pm}+A_{\pm}D_{\pm}A_{\pm}^\top
 =\operatorname{diag}\!\left(1,\tfrac34\right)
  +\operatorname{diag}\!\left(0,\tfrac14\right)
 =I_2.
\]
Both points satisfy \(\rho(A_{\pm})=0<1\) and \(D_{\pm}\succ0\), while their transfers are \(z/2\) and \(-z/2\).  They are interior transfer-distinct witnesses, so the exact two-copy test cannot return a singleton or an endpoint artifact.

For the second check, let \(d=2\), \(m=2\), and let \((A,D)\) be any compatible point with \(A_{21}\neq0\).  The support zeros and lower-triangular form are preserved by \(A\mapsto-A\), as are stability and positivity of \(D\), and
\[
 (-A)^2=A^2,
 \qquad
 D+(-A)D(-A)^\top=D+ADA^\top.
\]
Thus \((-A,D)\) is a second compatible point for the same \((B,Q)\).  With \(p=A_{21}\), \(q=A_{22}\), \(p'=-p\), and \(q'=-q\),
\[
 \Delta(p,q,-p,-q)
 =(2p)^2+\{p(-q)-(-p)q\}^2
 =4p^2>0.
\]
Hence every such nonzero-edge two-variable \(m=2\) case retains the global sign pair, as required.

Fix a data-generating law \(P_\star\) in the compact stable class, write its fine-grid parameters as \((A_\star,D_\star)\), and denote its stationary coarse moments by \((M_{0\star},M_{1\star})\). Define
\[
 E_n:=\{(M_{0\star},M_{1\star})\in\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha)\}.
\]
The compact-class lower-triangular restriction gives
\[
 \det(\lambda I_d-A_\star)=\prod_{i\in V}\{\lambda-(A_\star)_{ii}\},
\]
so the eigenvalues of \(A_\star\) are its diagonal entries. Its stability-margin restriction therefore implies
\[
 \rho(A_\star)=\max_{i\in V}|(A_\star)_{ii}|
 \leq 1-\gamma<1.
\]
Thus the stability premise of \(\mathrm{lem{:}coarse\mbox{-}law\mbox{-}reduction}\) holds. That lemma gives \(M_{0\star}\succ0\) and
\[
 M_{1\star}=A_\star^mM_{0\star},
 \qquad
 M_{0\star}=A_\star^mM_{0\star}(A_\star^m)^\top
 +\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}A_\star^rD_\star(A_\star^r)^\top.
\]
Membership of \(P_\star\) in the class of \(\mathrm{def{:}compact\mbox{-}class}\) supplies, separately, the lower-triangular zero restrictions, the graph-support zero restrictions, the bounds
\(\max_i|(A_\star)_{ii}|\leq1-\gamma\) and
\(\max_{i,j}|(A_\star)_{ij}|\leq L\), diagonality of \(D_\star\), and
\(d_{\min}I_d\preceq D_\star\preceq d_{\max}I_d\). Hence every defining constraint of \(\mathcal R_n\) in \(\mathrm{def{:}inverse\mbox{-}region}\) is satisfied on \(E_n\), with existential witnesses \((M_0,M_1)=(M_{0\star},M_{1\star})\). Therefore
\[
 E_n\subseteq\{(A_\star,D_\star)\in\mathcal R_n\}.
\]
For \(z\in\mathbb T\), the stability margin gives
\[
 |1-(A_\star)_{vv}z|
 \geq1-|(A_\star)_{vv}||z|
 \geq\gamma>0,
\]
so the queried transfer is well defined. By \(\mathrm{def{:}transfer\mbox{-}confidence\mbox{-}set}\),
\[
 \{(A_\star,D_\star)\in\mathcal R_n\}
 \subseteq
 \left\{z\longmapsto\frac{(A_\star)_{vu}z}
 {1-(A_\star)_{vv}z}\in\mathcal C_n^h\right\}.
\]
Combining the last two inclusions with
\(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}moment\mbox{-}box}\) yields
\[
 P_\star\{h_{uv}\in\mathcal C_n^h\}
 \geq P_\star(E_n)\geq1-\alpha.
\]
Since \(P_\star\) was arbitrary, the bound is uniform over the compact class. The argument tests all defining equations of the inverse region simultaneously; it neither selects a matrix-root branch nor divides by a divided difference.

For the last assertion, suppose that two compact-class members \((A^{(1)},D^{(1)})\) and \((A^{(2)},D^{(2)})\) induce the same stationary coarse moment pair \((M_0,M_1)\), and let their queried transfers be \(h_{uv}^{(1)}\neq h_{uv}^{(2)}\). On the common event
\[
 E_n^{\circ}:=\{(M_0,M_1)\in\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha)\},
\]
the coarse-law identities and the class restrictions, applied once for each \(k\in\{1,2\}\), imply
\[
 (A^{(k)},D^{(k)})\in\mathcal R_n.
\]
The transfer-set definition then gives
\[
 \{h_{uv}^{(1)},h_{uv}^{(2)}\}\subseteq\mathcal C_n^h
 \quad\text{on }E_n^{\circ}.
\]
Thus both unequal, actually attained transfers remain in the confidence set whenever the common moment pair is in the moment box, proving the claimed possible noncontraction.

Fix \(n\geq3\) and a data-generating law \(P\) in the compact stable class. Equip the trajectory space
\(\Omega_n=\mathbb R^{(n+1)d}\) with its Borel \(\sigma\)-field and define
\[
 \widehat K_{\Sigma,n}:\Omega_n\longrightarrow(0,\infty),
 \qquad
 \widehat K_{\Sigma,n}(w):=K_\Sigma.
\]
This constant map is measurable: for each Borel set \(E\subseteq(0,\infty)\), its inverse image is \(\Omega_n\) if \(K_\Sigma\in E\), and is empty otherwise.

Let \(\Sigma_{n,P}:=\operatorname{Cov}_P(W_n)\). The coarse spectral-density resolvent bound in
\(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}moment\mbox{-}box}\), applied with the restrictions collected in \(\mathrm{def{:}compact\mbox{-}class}\), gives
\[
 0\preceq\Sigma_{n,P}\preceq K_\Sigma I_{(n+1)d},
 \qquad
 \|\Sigma_{n,P}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq K_\Sigma
 =\widehat K_{\Sigma,n}(W_n)
 \quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
Thus the proposed envelope dominates the trajectory covariance simultaneously over the compact class at every finite sample size.

To check its compatibility with the spectral-split handle, fix a symmetric lag-moment matrix \(H_{\ell ij}\) from \(\mathrm{Hell}\), and write its spectral decomposition as
\(H_{\ell ij}=H_{\ell ij}^{+}-H_{\ell ij}^{-}\), where
\(H_{\ell ij}^{+}\succeq0\) and \(H_{\ell ij}^{-}\succeq0\). For either \(s\in\{+,-\}\), covariance domination and congruence by \((H_{\ell ij}^{s})^{1/2}\) give
\[
 \operatorname{tr}(H_{\ell ij}^{s}\Sigma_{n,P})
 =\operatorname{tr}\!\left((H_{\ell ij}^{s})^{1/2}
 \Sigma_{n,P}(H_{\ell ij}^{s})^{1/2}\right)
 \leq K_\Sigma\operatorname{tr}(H_{\ell ij}^{s}).
\]
Submultiplicativity of the operator norm also gives
\[
 \bigl\|\Sigma_{n,P}^{1/2}H_{\ell ij}^{s}
 \Sigma_{n,P}^{1/2}\bigr\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq\|\Sigma_{n,P}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \|H_{\ell ij}^{s}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq K_\Sigma\|H_{\ell ij}^{s}\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Hence both spectral parts are controlled by the measurable constant envelope. Recombining the two parts recovers the same deterministic two-sided calibration already certified by
\(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}moment\mbox{-}box}\).

Define, for every realized trajectory,
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^M(\alpha):=\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha),
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal R}_n:=\mathcal R_n,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^h:=\mathcal C_n^h.
\]
For each \((\ell,i,j)\in\{0,1\}\times V\times V\), the coordinate interval of the first set is therefore exactly
\[
 \operatorname{Out}_N\!\left((\widehat M_\ell)_{ij},
 2K_\Sigma\left\{
 \sqrt{\frac{\log(4d^2/\alpha)}{n}}
 +\frac{\log(4d^2/\alpha)}{n}\right\}\right),
\]
which is the corresponding deterministic-\(K_\Sigma\) interval in
\(\mathrm{def{:}moment\mbox{-}box}\). The widths are consequently equal for every sample point, so
\[
 P\!\left\{\text{all fallback coordinate widths are no larger than
 their deterministic-\(K_\Sigma\) counterparts}\right\}=1.
\]

The equality of the two moment regions and
\(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}moment\mbox{-}box}\) imply
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cmp}}}
 P\{(M_0,M_1)\in\widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^M(\alpha)\}
 =
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cmp}}}
 P\{(M_0,M_1)\in\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha)\}
 \geq1-\alpha,
\]
where \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cmp}}\) denotes the fixed compact class of
\(\mathrm{def{:}compact\mbox{-}class}\). Each coordinate endpoint is rational by the defining guarantee of \(\operatorname{Out}_N\). Finally,
\(\widetilde{\mathcal R}_n=\mathcal R_n\) leaves every polynomial equality and inequality in \(\mathrm{def{:}inverse\mbox{-}region}\) unchanged, while
\(\widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^h=\mathcal C_n^h\) leaves its transfer projection unchanged. Thus the rational encoding and exact branch-free semialgebraic inversion are preserved. By \(\mathrm{thm{:}global\mbox{-}honest\mbox{-}inversion}\), the same equalities also retain finite-sample transfer coverage. All comparisons are equalities, so the proof makes no claim of strict adaptive improvement.

theorem.statement:
The adaptive-calibration question has an affirmative answer in its literal weak \emph{no wider} sense. For every \(n\geq3\), the spectral-split handle \(\mathrm{CalHandle}\) admits the measurable constant covariance envelope \(\widehat K_{\Sigma,n}\equiv K_\Sigma\) and the choices
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^M(\alpha)=\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha),
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal R}_n=\mathcal R_n,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^h=\mathcal C_n^h.
\]
For every law in the compact class, every coordinate interval then has exactly the width of its deterministic-\(K_\Sigma\) counterpart with probability one; consequently the coordinatewise no-wider probability equals one for every \(n\), and hence tends to one for every interior regular law in that class. The moment region has finite-sample coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over the compact class, its endpoints are rationally outward rounded, and its exact branch-free semialgebraic inverse is unchanged. This answer certifies equality of widths and does not certify a strict adaptive improvement.
theorem.proof_tex: Apply \(\mathrm{thm{:}adaptive\mbox{-}calibration\mbox{-}fallback}\) at each \(n\geq3\). That theorem proves that the constant map \(w\mapsto K_\Sigma\) is measurable and is an admissible covariance envelope for the spectral split, and it establishes the three displayed equalities of random regions. Equality of the moment regions gives equality, sample by sample, of every coordinate interval and therefore makes the coordinatewise no-wider event the whole trajectory sample space. Its probability is one under every compact-class law for every \(n\), so the probability sequence converges to one under every interior regular law contained in that class. The same theorem supplies uniform finite-sample moment coverage, rational outward rounding, and preservation of the exact semialgebraic inverse. Because the construction uses equality with the deterministic region, no strict width reduction follows.

proofs.proof_tex:
Formally specialize Definition~\texttt{def:compatible-fiber} and Definition~\texttt{def:certificate} to \(m=1\).  Let \((A,D)\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\).  The first compatibility equation in Definition~\texttt{def:compatible-fiber} gives
\[
B=A^1=A.
\]
The second compatibility equation in that definition, together with \(A^0=I_d\), gives
\[
Q=\sum_{r=0}^{1-1}A^rD(A^r)^\top
  =A^0D(A^0)^\top
  =D.
\]
Therefore every member of \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\) equals \((B,Q)\), so the fiber has at most one member.

Conversely, substitute \((A,D)=(B,Q)\) into Definition~\texttt{def:compatible-fiber}.  The two coarse equations then hold identically, because \(B^1=B\) and \(B^0Q(B^0)^\top=Q\).  The remaining defining conditions hold if and only if
\[
B_{ij}=0\quad(i<j),
\qquad
B_{ij}=0\quad(i>j\ \text{and}\ j\to i\notin G),
\]
\[
\max_i|B_{ii}|<1,
\qquad
Q_{ij}=0\quad(i\ne j),
\qquad
Q\succ0.
\]
These are precisely the fine-grid compatibility constraints obtained by specializing that definition to \(m=1\).  Hence
\[
\mathcal S(B,Q;G)=
\begin{cases}
\{(B,Q)\},&\text{if all the displayed compatibility constraints hold},\\
\varnothing,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

It remains to verify the algorithmic output asserted in the proposition.  Under the same specialization, every diagonal root equation enumerated by \(\operatorname{Cert}_{uv,1,G}(B,Q)\) is
\[
a_{ii}^{,1}=B_{ii},
\]
and thus has the unique real solution \(a_{ii}=B_{ii}\).  By the declared definition of the divided-difference coefficient,
\[
C_1(x,y)=\sum_{r=0}^{0}x^r y^{0-r}=1.
\]
A nondecreasing walk of length one has at most one strict increase.  Consequently, the index set in the definition of the indirect-path remainder is empty and
\[
R_{vu,1}(A)=0.
\]
At each lower-triangular coordinate processed by the graph recursion in Definition~\texttt{def:certificate}, the root identity therefore reduces to
\[
B_{vu}=A_{vu}C_1(A_{vv},A_{uu})+R_{vu,1}(A)=A_{vu}.
\]
Thus every divided-difference coefficient is nonzero, the recursive enumeration has the unique transition candidate \(A=B\), and the coarse covariance equation has the unique innovation candidate \(D=Q\).  The exact compatibility test rejects this candidate exactly when one of the defining fiber constraints fails.  In that case the preceding fiber characterization gives \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)=\varnothing\), so the certificate returns incompatibility.  Otherwise it accepts the unique compatible pair \((B,Q)\).

In the latter case, both copies in the certificate's two-copy transfer-inequality system must equal \((B,Q)\); hence that inequality system is infeasible.  The common-transfer branch consequently returns, using the declared definition of \(h_{uv}\),
\[
h_{uv}(z)
=\frac{A_{vu}z}{1-A_{vv}z}
=\frac{B_{vu}z}{1-B_{vv}z}.
\]
Accepted compatibility also gives \(|B_{vv}|<1\).  Since \(z\in\mathbb T\) implies \(|z|=1\),
\[
|B_{vv}z|=|B_{vv}|<1,
\]
so \(1-B_{vv}z\ne0\).  The returned rational function is therefore well defined on \(\mathbb T\), and, because \(A=B\), it is exactly the unaliased direct fine-grid process transfer.  This proves every assertion of the proposition.
